newsitem.title: UK: EMI posts profit, shakes up North American unit.
newsitem.headline: EMI posts profit, shakes up North American unit.

text.p: British music company EMI Group Plc reported a slight increase in profits Tuesday and announced a streamlining of its North American music operations.
EMI, one of the six major companies dominating the global music industry, said its pre-tax profit for the year ended March 31 totalled 284 million pounds ($466 million).
The results were hurt, however, by a provision of 117 million pounds ($192 million) to cover the cost of office closures and asset write-offs relating to the North American restructuring.
The restructuring is designed to cut costs, improve links with other parts of the group and begin a process of management renewal, EMI said.

The company, which has the Beatles catalogue and modern-day artists such as The Spice Girls on its roster, also said it planned to return up to 10 percent of its market value to shareholders -- a total of around 500 million pounds ($820 million).
EMI said it planned to present proposals to return capital to shareholders at its annual meeting July 18 and implement them shortly afterwards.

Ken Berry, who heads EMI Music International and Virgin Records, was appointed worldwide president of EMI Recorded Music, adding control of the EMI Capitol label to his existing responsibilities. He will continue to report to Jim Fifield, CEO of EMI Music.
